rows.title: Referential integrity bugs related to catalog, basket, and order
rows.excerpt:
Hi,

There appears to be code logic that breaks referential integrity constraints and causes inconsistencies during execution. I would like to share this to understand if the issues are valid in the context of the application, and whether these bugs could be addressed. Thank you in advance.

The issues are related to the data associations established across the catalog, basket, and order microservices, where the baskets and orders contain item IDs that reference the item IDs of the corresponding products in the catalog.

Below are the steps to reproduce the bugs and their potential impact on the system.

### Scenario 1: Catalog-Basket

**Steps to reproduce bugs:**

Consider a client that manages its cart items via the Web App and an administrator who manages the catalog via the REST API.

The flow of requests is illustrated in a shared [figure](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tvxXGYsScQAVJruN8ydk3aSRd-IpnS0r/view?usp=sharing). The illustrated databases contain data from the original application. For simplicity, only the catalog and basket services are represented, along with the most relevant calls and arguments.

- The client adds items to the basket. _(fig. calls 1-3)_
- The admin lists all items from the catalog to get the IDs of the items. _(fig. calls 4-5)_
- The admin deletes an item from the catalog. _(fig. calls 6-7)_
- The client proceeds to the checkout. _(fig. calls 8-12)_

**Description of the bugs:**

**1. Absence of cascading delete:** each basket item contains the ID of the corresponding catalog item, resembling a foreign key. However, when the catalog item is deleted (fig. call 7), this action is not propagated to the basket, leaving a reference that is no longer valid.

During checkout (or even when viewing the cart), the web app's [`FetchBasketItemsAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/1b2698cd83ed5c9e00a2fa954f2586c87022c431/src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs#L117) receives data from querying the basket (fig. calls 9-10, where the returned item IDs contain the deleted item ID) that is inconsistent with the data obtained from querying the catalog (fig. calls 11-12, where the returned items do not contain the deleted item).

The web app's [`FetchBasketItemsAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/1b2698cd83ed5c9e00a2fa954f2586c87022c431/src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs#L117)  expects that every basket item is present in the ret

Introduce pluggable functional test modes (Aspire, RepositoryMock, EfCoreInMemory, Testcontainers, and messaging variants) for Catalog and Ordering via a shared Testing.Common library. Extract ICatalogRepository from Catalog.API to enable in-memory persistence swaps, add Serilog logging to ServiceDefaults, fix integration event type discovery under WebApplicationFactory, and add runsettings plus xUnit traits for filtering tests by mode.

# eShop Multi-Mode Functional Testing

> Architecture and design reference for eShop's pluggable functional test infrastructure,
> covering test modes, messaging validation, and related production changes.

---

## Overview

eShop functional tests use a **pluggable test-mode architecture** shared across Catalog and Ordering microservices. The main themes are:

1. **Multi-mode test infrastructure** (Aspire, mocks, in-memory EF, Testcontainers)
2. **Messaging/outbox integration tests** (RabbitMQ + transactional outbox)
3. **Catalog API repository extraction** (to enable swappable persistence in tests)
4. **Structured logging** (Serilog in production + rich test logging)
5. **Integration event discovery fix** (works under test host)

---

## Feature 1: Multi-Mode Functional Test Framework

### What Changed

The old pattern — one `WebApplicationFactory` fixture hard-wired to Aspire + PostgreSQL — was replaced with a **pluggable test-mode architecture** shared across Catalog and Ordering.

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Single `CatalogApiFixture` / `OrderingApiFixture` at project root | Mode-aware fixtures under `Fixture/` |
| Always Aspire + Docker | 4–6 modes per service |
| `IClassFixture<...>` per test class | `CatalogApiTestSession` / `OrderingApiTestSession` as assembly fixture |
| Hard-coded DB assertions | Persistence helpers that work per mode |

### Test Modes

| Mode | Infrastructure | Persistence | External Deps |
|------|----------------|-------------|---------------|

rows.title: Fix KeyNotFoundException and NullReferenceException when catalog items are deleted
rows.excerpt:
When catalog items are deleted, basket items and orders retain references to non-existent product IDs, causing the WebApp to crash with `KeyNotFoundException` during basket operations and the Catalog API to crash with `NullReferenceException` during order validation.

## Changes

**BasketState.cs**
- Replace dictionary indexer with `TryGetValue()` to handle missing catalog items
- Filter out basket items for deleted products instead of crashing
- Add warning log when skipping items

**OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationIntegrationEventHandler.cs**
- Handle null catalog items during order validation
- Treat deleted products as out of stock to reject orders gracefully
- Add warning log for missing products

## Example

Before:
```csharp
var catalogItem = catalogItems[item.ProductId]; // throws KeyNotFoundException
```

After:
```csharp
if (!catalogItems.TryGetValue(item.ProductId, out var catalogItem))
{
    logger.LogWarning("Basket item with ProductId {ProductId} not found in catalog and will be skipped", item.ProductId);
    continue;
}
```

This defensive approach allows the system to continue functioning when data inconsistencies occur across microservices, avoiding the need for distributed transaction coordination.
